subject: Request: approval for Lynx contract - indemnity escrow & warranty carveout
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lynxsystems.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed redlines and onboarding terms

Ben —

Thanks again for the demo. Our procurement team asked us to send a single document with the contract comments and a couple of commercial asks so we can get legal and procurement aligned. Attached is our redline (Lynx_Redlines_2028-11-29.pdf). The headline items: 

- One-time onboarding discount: 25% off first-year fees (we cited comparable platform deals)
- Escrow for customer source data used to seed the model training (we'll need a statement of what gets escrowed and for how long)
- Indemnity: want mutual indemnity language plus carveouts for third-party data claims; also asking to remove sublimit for IP claims
- Warranty: request a performance warranty for data integrity and an SLA credit table tied to uptime; also want an extended warranty period for integration-related defects

We know some of these are non-standard. Can you confirm who at Redwood signs off on this scope? If exec sign-off is required, please advise next steps.

Thanks,
Daniel
Lynx Systems

P.S. CC'ing Olivia from procurement for timelines.
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lynxsystems.com>
Cc: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@lynxsystems.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines and onboarding terms

Daniel —

Got the redline and the asks. Appreciate the clarity. I'm pulling together the internal stakeholders now (legal and revenue ops). High level answers up front: we can usually accept mutual indemnity with limited exceptions, and we have an established process for escrow requests but scope will matter. The 25% onboarding discount is larger than our standard deal desk thresholds, so I will need exec approval for anything over 15%.

I'll send you a risk summary and a target counter this afternoon once I have legal input. Can you confirm target signature date? That will help prioritize.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: SOW_Lynx_v3.docx (draft SOW), pricing_summary_lynx.xlsx (current pricing model)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-29T13:22:00-08:00
Subject: FWD: Lynx redlines — need legal + deal desk guidance (escrow / indemnity / warranty)

Marissa / Laura —

Forwarding Lynx's redlines. Key non-standard asks summarized below: 

1) 25% onboarding discount (one-time, applied to first-year subscription). Our normal max without exec ok is 15%.
2) Escrow of customer source data used to seed any model training — they want explicit escrow terms and the ability to pull data if we stop servicing.
3) Indemnity: they want mutual breadth and removal of the sublimit on IP. Also request carveouts for third-party data claims.
4) Warranty: they want a performance warranty tied to data integrity and an extended defect warranty for integration items.

Suggested mitigations I'm proposing while you review: 
- Offer a 20% onboarding credit instead of 25% contingent on an escrow arrangement with limited scope (only ingestion snapshots) and a time-limited holdback (6 months).
- Accept mutual indemnity but keep IP claims subject to the standard sublimit; allow narrow carveouts for third-party data but require documented provenance and indemnity from the customer if they supply third-party data.
- Warranty: limit to our standard service commitments with a small SLA credit schedule; decline an extended integration warranty but offer 30 days of post-integration remediation support.

This will exceed my deal desk pricing authority; if legal is comfortable with the indemnity/warranty framing, we'll need exec approval on the 20% vs their 25% and the elevated liability cap for IP if legal recommends.

Can you confirm if the legal position below is acceptable and whether we should route to Markus for sign-off?

Thanks,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-11-30T10:09:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Lynx redlines — legal analysis and recommended approvals

Ben / Laura —

Quick read on the redlines and Ben's mitigation proposal. High level legal guidance: 

- Indemnity: We can accept a mutual indemnity. However, removing the IP sublimit materially increases commercial risk. Recommend keeping a sublimit but increasing it to $2,000,000 for this account (justified by ARR and strategic value) if exec approves. Require that any customer-provided third-party dataset be accompanied by written provenance and indemnity from the customer.

- Escrow: Escrow of raw customer source data is acceptable only under strict controls. We propose: escrow to a neutral third-party escrow agent, scope limited to ingestion snapshots used to reproduce a customer's environment (no derived models), retention capped at 12 months post-contract termination, and explicit deletion certification. Also require fees (one-time admin) to cover the escrow agent.

- Warranty: We should not accept an open-ended performance warranty. Offer a narrow warranty around uptime and non-corruption of ingested data with SLA credits as liquidated damages. For integration defects, offer a 30-day remediation period post-go-live and an optional extended support add-on for purchase.

Because the IP sublimit change and 20%+ discount exceed standard tolerances, this needs CM-level or CRO sign-off. Markus, cc'd, please advise if you will approve the $2M IP sublimit + 20% onboarding credit under the proposed escrow and provenance controls.

Marissa
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal_summary_notes.txt (internal)
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Lynx redlines — legal analysis and recommended approvals

Folks —

I've reviewed Marissa's notes and Ben's commercial ask. Given the strategic nature of Lynx (pilot scope + potential expansion), I will sign off with the following conditions: 

1) One-time onboarding credit: approve 20% (counter to their 25%). No other price concessions.
2) IP sublimit: increase to $2,000,000 as Marissa recommends, but capped only for claims arising from Redwood's own code/model IP; any customer-originated IP claim remains subject to standard indemnity carveouts.
3) Escrow: approve the neutral-agent escrow with the controls Marissa listed (scope-limited snapshots, 12-month retention post-termination, deletion certification). Legal to include escrow fees as a pass-through to Lynx.
4) Warranty: limited to SLA uptime commitments (99.5% target) with SLA credit schedule and 30-day integration remediation. No open-ended performance warranty.

Marissa / Laura — please draft the side letter documenting these items and the DocuSign package. Ben — communicate the counter and the DocuSign link to Lynx and confirm acceptance timeline.

Markus
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@lynxsystems.com>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@lynxsystems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-12-02T10:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed redlines and onboarding terms — Redwood counter and next steps

Daniel / Olivia —

Thanks for the patience. Redwood can accept the majority of your requests with the following counter (approved by our CRO):

- One-time onboarding credit: 20% off first-year subscription (company-approved final).
- Indemnity: mutual indemnity accepted. IP sublimit will be $2,000,000 (limited as noted to Redwood-origin IP) and customer-provided third-party data requires written provenance + customer indemnity.
- Escrow: we will use a neutral third-party escrow agent; scope limited to ingestion snapshots, retention capped at 12 months post-termination, and we will require a one-time escrow admin fee (passed through).
- Warranty: limited to SLA (99.5% uptime target) with SLA credit table; 30-day remediation window for integration defects; extended support available as paid add-on.

I've attached the updated SOW and the redlines for your review (Lynx_Redlines_2028-11-29.pdf, SOW_Lynx_v3.docx). I'll share a DocuSign package with the side letter and updated terms by EOD — please confirm target signature by 2028-12-09 to keep the current onboarding timeline.

Best,
Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/redwood/LYNX-1543
